s0201.literal: [30] In the twelfth year he died, aged thirteen.
s0201.idiomatic: [30] In the twelfth year he died, aged thirteen.

s0202.literal: Posthumously granted palace attendant, central-secure general, and director of works; posthumous title Kang-jian.
s0202.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant, central-secure general, and director of works, with the posthumous title Kang-jian.

s0204.literal: Xiaokuan in the first year of Zhide succeeded to the princedom of Hedong.
s0204.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 Xiaokuan succeeded as prince of Hedong.

s0205.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass; in the Daye era of Sui he was magistrate of Wencheng.
s0205.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass; under Sui's Daye era he served as magistrate of Wencheng.

s0206.literal: Prince of Jinxi Shuwén, styled Zicai, was the twelfth son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0206.idiomatic: Prince of Jinxi Shuwén, styled Zicai, was Emperor Gaozong's twelfth son.

s0207.literal: By nature frivolous and rash, he loved empty reputation and was somewhat versed in books and histories.
s0207.idiomatic: He was frivolous and vain, fond of empty reputation, and had some learning in books and histories.

s0208.literal: In the seventh year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Jinxi.
s0208.idiomatic: In Taijian year 7 he was made prince of Jinxi.

s0209.literal: Soon he was palace attendant, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and general who spreads grace, with aides and clerks.
s0209.idiomatic: He was soon palace attendant and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, with the title general who spreads grace and a full staff.

s0210.literal: His title was advanced to general of the light chariot and inspector of Yangzhou.
s0210.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the light chariot and inspector of Yangzhou.

s0211.literal: [31] In the first year of Zhide he was given the staff and made area commander over military affairs of Jiangzhou and inspector of Jiangzhou.
s0211.idiomatic: [31] In Zhide year 1 he received the staff as area commander over Jiangzhou and inspector of Jiang.

s0212.literal: In the second year he was moved to general of trusted might and area commander over the four provinces Xiang, Heng, Wu, and Gui, and inspector of Xiangzhou.
s0212.idiomatic: In year 2 he became general of trusted might and area commander over Xiang, Heng, Wu, and Gui, with the post of inspector of Xiang.

s0213.literal: In the second year of Zhenming, when his term expired, he was summoned as palace attendant and general of steadfast resolve, his aides and clerks as before.
s0213.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 2, when his term ended, he was recalled as palace attendant and general of steadfast resolve, staff unchanged.

s0214.literal: Before he returned, the Sui army crossed the Yangtze and broke Taicheng; the Sui commander of the eastern Han route, the Prince of Qin, reached Hankou.
s0214.idiomatic: Before he could return, Sui forces crossed the Yangtze and took Taicheng; the Prince of Qin, commander of the eastern Han route, reached Hankou.

s0215.literal: At that time Shuwén was returning from Xiangzhou to court and reached Bazhou; he then led Bazhou inspector Bi Bao and others to request surrender, sending a letter to the Prince of Qin saying: "I venture to observe that Heaven has no second sun, and the sequence of dark and bright does not err; the land has no second king, and the places of high and low are thereby set apart.
s0215.idiomatic: Shuwén was then returning from Xiang to court and reached Bazhou; he led Bazhou inspector Bi Bao and others to surrender, writing to the Prince of Qin, "Heaven has but one sun and the order of night and day never fails; the realm has but one king and rank is thereby fixed.

s0216.literal: Now carriage and writing are unified and culture and tracks are one; I dare lay open my red sincerity and declare my bent knee."
s0216.idiomatic: Now empire and script are one and the ways of court and countryside are joined; I dare lay bare my loyalty and bow the knee."

s0217.literal: The Prince of Qin received the letter and sent Xingjun's director of the ministry of personnel Liu Zhuang, with staff of the prince's headquarters and others, to Bazhou to welcome and comfort Shuwén.
s0217.idiomatic: The prince received the letter and sent Liu Zhuang of the ministry of personnel, with headquarters staff, to Bazhou to welcome Shuwén.

s0218.literal: Shuwén thereupon, with Bi Bao, Jingzhou inspector Chen Ji, and civil and military officers, went to Hankou; the Prince of Qin all treated them generously and lodged them in the guest house.
s0218.idiomatic: Shuwén then went to Hankou with Bi Bao, Jingzhou inspector Chen Ji, and his civil and military officers; the prince received them generously and lodged them in the guest quarters.

s0219.literal: In the third month of the ninth year of Sui's Kaihuang era the armies returned in triumph; Emperor Wen personally went to the hot springs to reward them; Shuwén, with Chen Ji, Zhou Luohou, Xun Fashang, and the other submitters, were seen along the route.
s0219.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaihuang year 9 the armies returned in triumph; Emperor Wen went in person to the hot springs to reward them, and Shuwén, Chen Ji, Zhou Luohou, Xun Fashang, and the other submitters were presented along the road.

s0220.literal: Several days later Shuwén followed Houzhu and the kings, marquises, generals, and ministers, with chariots, robes, astronomical charts and records, and the rest, each in order and rank; iron cavalry surrounded them as they followed the Prince of Jin, the Prince of Qin, and the others in presenting triumph and entering, arrayed in the court of the ancestral temple.
s0220.idiomatic: Days later Shuwén followed Houzhu and the princes, marquises, generals, and ministers, with chariots, regalia, charts, and records, each in rank; iron cavalry ringed them as they marched with the princes of Jin and Qin in triumphal entry and were ranged in the temple court.

s0221.literal: The next day Emperor Wen of Sui sat at Guangyang Gate to observe; Shuwén again followed Houzhu to the south of the audience hall; Emperor Wen had Secretariat Director Li Delin proclaim the decree, rebuking their ruler and ministers for failing to support one another and thereby bringing ruin.
s0221.idiomatic: The next day Emperor Wen sat at Guangyang Gate to review them; Shuwén again followed Houzhu to the south of the audience hall while Li Delin, director of the secretariat, proclaimed a decree rebuking ruler and ministers for failing one another and bringing the state to ruin.

s0222.literal: Houzhu and his ministers all bowed in shame and fear, none daring to look up; Shuwén alone was pleased and had the air of self-satisfaction.
s0222.idiomatic: Houzhu and his ministers bowed in shame and fear, none daring to raise their eyes; Shuwén alone looked pleased, as if satisfied with himself.

s0223.literal: Sixteen days later he submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly at Bazhou I had already sent my submission first; I beg to know this circumstance and hope for an exceptional case."
s0223.idiomatic: Sixteen days later he memorialized, "At Bazhou I had already submitted first; I beg that this be known and that I receive exceptional treatment."

s0224.literal: Though Emperor Wen resented his disloyalty, he was then wishing to soothe the lands south of the Yangtze and therefore granted an establishment and made him inspector of Yizhou.
s0224.idiomatic: Though the emperor resented his disloyalty, he still wished to soothe the south and therefore granted him an establishment and made him inspector of Yi.

s0225.literal: Prince of Huainan Shubiao, styled Zihua, was the thirteenth son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0225.idiomatic: Prince of Huainan Shubiao, styled Zihua, was Emperor Gaozong's thirteenth son.

s0226.literal: In youth intelligent and clever, skilled at literary composition.
s0226.idiomatic: As a youth he was clever and skilled at writing.

s0227.literal: In the eighth year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Huainan.
s0227.idiomatic: In Taijian year 8 he was made prince of Huainan.

s0228.literal: Soon he was palace attendant and general of humane might, with aides and clerks.
s0228.idiomatic: He was soon palace attendant and general of humane might, with a staff.

s0229.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass and died at Chang'an.
s0229.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass and died at Chang'an.

s0230.literal: Prince of Shixing Shuzhong, styled Zihou, was the fourteenth son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0230.idiomatic: Prince of Shixing Shuzhong, styled Zihou, was Emperor Gaozong's fourteenth son.

s0231.literal: By nature simple and plain, without arts or skills.
s0231.idiomatic: He was plain by nature and without special talents.

s0232.literal: When Emperor Gaozong died, Prince of Shixing Shuling rebelled and was executed; that year Shuzhong was established as Prince of Shixing to continue the line of Prince Zhao-lie.
s0232.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, Prince of Shixing Shuling rebelled and was put to death; that year Shuzhong was made prince of Shixing to continue Prince Zhao-lie's line.

s0233.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was general of humane might and inspector of Yangzhou, with aides and clerks.
s0233.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he was general of humane might and inspector of Yangzhou, with a staff.

s0234.literal: In the second year he was given the added staff and made area commander over military affairs of Jiangzhou and inspector of Jiangzhou.
s0234.idiomatic: In year 2 he received the staff as area commander over Jiangzhou and inspector of Jiang.

s0235.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass.
s0235.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass.

s0236.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was vice director of the grand treasury and died.
s0236.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye era he was vice director of the grand treasury and died.

s0237.literal: Prince of Xunyang Shuyan, styled Zisi, was the fifteenth son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0237.idiomatic: Prince of Xunyang Shuyan, styled Zisi, was Emperor Gaozong's fifteenth son.

s0238.literal: By nature grave and weighty, his bearing and conduct were square and upright.
s0238.idiomatic: Grave in nature, his bearing was square and upright.

s0239.literal: When Houzhu succeeded to the throne he was established as Prince of Xunyang.
s0239.idiomatic: When Houzhu took the throne he was made prince of Xunyang.

s0240.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was palace attendant and general of humane martiality, with aides and clerks.
s0240.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he was palace attendant and general of humane martiality, with a staff.

s0241.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass and soon died.
s0241.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass and soon died.

s0242.literal: In year three, when the Sui army crossed the Yangtze and broke Taicheng, the former inspector Prince of Jinxi Shuwén returned to Bazhou and, with Bazhou inspector Bi Bao and Jingzhou inspector Chen Ji, all surrendered.
s0242.idiomatic: In year 3, when Sui forces crossed the Yangtze and took Taicheng, the former inspector Prince of Jinxi Shuwén returned to Bazhou and surrendered with Bazhou inspector Bi Bao and Jingzhou inspector Chen Ji.

s0243.literal: The Sui campaign commander Duke of Qinghe Yang Su led troops down Jingmen and separately sent his general Pang Hui with troops to overrun the land, south to Xiangzhou; within the city none had a mind to hold firm, and on the appointed day they requested surrender.
s0243.idiomatic: Sui commander Duke of Qinghe Yang Su marched down Jingmen and sent his general Pang Hui south to Xiangzhou; none in the city would stand firm, and they asked to surrender on the set day.

s0244.literal: Shushen thereupon set wine and feasted the civil and military officers; when the wine was deep, Shushen sighed and said, "The righteousness of ruler and minister ends here, does it not!"
s0244.idiomatic: Shushen then set wine for his civil and military officers; when they were deep in drink he sighed, "The bond of ruler and minister ends here, does it not!"

s0245.literal: Chief steward Xie Ji lay prostrate weeping; the Xiangzhou assistant for defense, Marquis of Suixing Zheng Lili, who was present, then rose and said, "When the lord is shamed the minister dies—are you alone not Chen ministers?
s0245.idiomatic: Chief steward Xie Ji lay prostrate weeping; Xiangzhou's assistant for defense, Marquis of Suixing Zheng Lili, who was present, rose and said, "When the lord is shamed the minister must die—are you not all Chen ministers?

s0246.literal: Now the realm has difficulty; this is truly the season to give one's life.
s0246.idiomatic: The realm is in peril; this is truly the hour to give one's life.

s0247.literal: Even if there is no success, one still shows the minister's integrity; beyond the Green Gate there is death one cannot refuse.
s0247.idiomatic: Even without success we may yet show a minister's integrity; beyond the Green Gate there is death one cannot refuse.

s0248.literal: Today's opportunity cannot be hesitated over; whoever follows afterward shall be beheaded."
s0248.idiomatic: Today's chance cannot be hesitated over; whoever holds back shall be beheaded."

s0249.literal: The crowd all promised; they then slaughtered a victim and formed an alliance.
s0249.idiomatic: All assented; they slaughtered a victim and swore an oath.

s0250.literal: They then sent a man to feign a surrender letter to Pang Hui; Hui believed it and, on the agreed day, entered; Shushen had armed men wait in ambush.
s0250.idiomatic: They sent a man with a false surrender letter to Pang Hui; Hui believed it and entered on the agreed day while Shushen's men lay in ambush.

s0251.literal: Hui ordered several hundred men to camp at the city gate; he himself led several tens of men into the hall; soon the ambush sprang, they bound Hui and paraded him, seized all his party, and beheaded them.
s0251.idiomatic: Hui left several hundred men at the gate and led a few dozen into the hall; the ambush sprang, they bound Hui and paraded him through the streets, seized his party, and beheaded them all.

s0252.literal: Shushen sat in the archery hall and gathered soldiers; within several days troops reached five thousand men.
s0252.idiomatic: Shushen sat in the archery hall and gathered troops; within days his force reached five thousand.

s0253.literal: Hengyang prefect Fan Tong and Wuzhou inspector Wu Juye both requested to come to the rescue.
s0253.idiomatic: Hengyang prefect Fan Tong and Wuzhou inspector Wu Juye both asked to march to his aid.

s0254.literal: Before they arrived, Sui sent Duke of Zhongmou Xue Zhou as inspector of Xiangzhou; hearing of Pang Hui's death, he asked for more troops, and Sui also sent campaign commander Liu Ren'en to rescue.
s0254.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Sui appointed Duke of Zhongmou Xue Zhou inspector of Xiang; hearing Pang Hui was dead, he asked for reinforcements, and Sui also sent campaign commander Liu Ren'en.

s0255.literal: Before they arrived, Xue Zhou's troops halted at Goose-Sheep Mountain; Shushen sent Zheng Lili and Fan Tong and others to resist them; a great battle was joined from dawn until the sun slanted, the Sui army resting and fighting in turns, while Zheng Lili's troops were few and could not match—thereupon they were greatly defeated.
s0255.idiomatic: Before reinforcements came, Xue Zhou halted at Goose-Sheep Mountain; Shushen sent Zheng Lili and Fan Tong to meet him. They fought from dawn until afternoon; the Sui rested and renewed the attack in turns, and Zheng Lili's few men could not hold—at last they were routed.

s0256.literal: Zhou took advantage of victory to enter the city and captured Shushen alive.
s0256.idiomatic: Zhou pressed his victory into the city and took Shushen alive.

s0257.literal: At that time Wu Juye led his host from Wuzhou to come to the rescue, crossed Hengqiao River, heard that Shushen had been defeated, and halted at Xinkang Ford.
s0257.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wu Juye marched from Wuzhou to aid him, crossed Hengqiao River, heard Shushen was beaten, and halted at Xinkang Ford.

s0258.literal: Sui commander Liu Ren'en's troops also reached Hengqiao, set camp by the water, faced one another for several days, then joined battle, and Juye was again defeated.
s0258.idiomatic: Liu Ren'en also reached Hengqiao, camped across the water, faced Juye for several days, then fought, and Juye was beaten again.

s0259.literal: Ren'en captured Shushen, Zheng Lili, Juye, and more than ten of their party; the Prince of Qin beheaded them at Hankou.
s0259.idiomatic: Ren'en took Shushen, Zheng Lili, Juye, and more than ten of their party; the Prince of Qin had them beheaded at Hankou.

s0261.literal: Prince of Yiyang Shuda, styled Zicong, was the seventeenth son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0261.idiomatic: Prince of Yiyang Shuda, styled Zicong, was Emperor Gaozong's seventeenth son.

s0262.literal: In the fourteenth year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Yiyang; soon he was general of martial humanity, with aides and clerks.
s0262.idiomatic: In Taijian year 14 he was made prince of Yiyang; soon he was general of martial humanity, with a staff.

s0263.literal: In the first year of Zhenming he was made metropolitan magistrate of Danyang.
s0263.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 1 he was made metropolitan magistrate of Danyang.

s0264.literal: In the third year he entered the pass.
s0264.idiomatic: In year 3 he entered the pass.

s0265.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was inner scribe and rose to transit prefect of Jiang commandery.
s0265.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye era he was inner scribe and rose to transit prefect of Jiang commandery.

s0266.literal: Prince of Bashan Shuxiong, styled Zimeng, was the eighteenth son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0266.idiomatic: Prince of Bashan Shuxiong, styled Zimeng, was Emperor Gaozong's eighteenth son.

s0267.literal: In the fourteenth year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Bashan.
s0267.idiomatic: In Taijian year 14 he was made prince of Bashan.

s0268.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass and died at Chang'an.
s0268.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass and died at Chang'an.

s0269.literal: Prince of Wuchang Shuyu, styled Zi'an, was the nineteenth son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0269.idiomatic: Prince of Wuchang Shuyu, styled Zi'an, was Emperor Gaozong's nineteenth son.

s0270.literal: In the fourteenth year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Wuchang; soon he was stalwart-martial general, with aides and clerks.
s0270.idiomatic: In Taijian year 14 he was made prince of Wuchang; soon he was stalwart-martial general, with a staff.

s0271.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass.
s0271.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass.

s0272.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was magistrate of Gaoyuan.
s0272.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Gaoyuan.

s0273.literal: Prince of Xiangdong Shuping, styled Zikang, was the twentieth son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0273.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangdong Shuping, styled Zikang, was Emperor Gaozong's twentieth son.

s0274.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was established as Prince of Xiangdong.
s0274.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he was made prince of Xiangdong.

s0275.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass.
s0275.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass.

s0276.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was magistrate of Husu.
s0276.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Husu.

s0277.literal: Prince of Linhe Shu'ao, styled Ziren, was the twenty-first son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0277.idiomatic: Prince of Linhe Shu'ao, styled Ziren, was Emperor Gaozong's twenty-first son.

s0278.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was established as Prince of Linhe; soon he was general of humane martiality, with aides and clerks.
s0278.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he was made prince of Linhe; soon he was general of humane martiality, with a staff.

s0279.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass.
s0279.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass.

s0280.literal: At the beginning of the Daye era of Sui he was granted the third rank of ceremonial parity.
s0280.idiomatic: At the opening of Sui's Daye era he was granted third-rank ceremonial parity.

s0281.literal: Prince of Yangshan Shuxuan, styled Zitong, was the twenty-second son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0281.idiomatic: Prince of Yangshan Shuxuan, styled Zitong, was Emperor Gaozong's twenty-second son.

s0282.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was established as Prince of Yangshan.
s0282.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he was made prince of Yangshan.

s0283.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass.
s0283.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass.

s0284.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was magistrate of Jingcheng.
s0284.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Jingcheng.

s0285.literal: Prince of Xiyang Shumu, styled Zihe, was the twenty-third son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0285.idiomatic: Prince of Xiyang Shumu, styled Zihe, was Emperor Gaozong's twenty-third son.

s0286.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was established as Prince of Xiyang.
s0286.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he was made prince of Xiyang.

s0287.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass and died at Chang'an.
s0287.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass and died at Chang'an.

s0288.literal: Prince of Nan'an Shujian, styled Ziyue, was the twenty-fourth son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0288.idiomatic: Prince of Nan'an Shujian, styled Ziyue, was Emperor Gaozong's twenty-fourth son.

s0289.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was established as Prince of Nan'an.
s0289.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he was made prince of Nan'an.

s0290.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass and died at Chang'an.
s0290.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass and died at Chang'an.

s0291.literal: Prince of Nan commandery Shucheng, styled Ziquan, was the twenty-fifth son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0291.idiomatic: Prince of Nan commandery Shucheng, styled Ziquan, was Emperor Gaozong's twenty-fifth son.

s0292.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was established as Prince of Nan commandery.
s0292.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he was made prince of Nan commandery.

s0293.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass.
s0293.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass.

s0294.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was magistrate of Lingwu.
s0294.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Lingwu.

s0295.literal: Prince of Yuanling Shuxing, styled Zitui, was the twenty-sixth son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0295.idiomatic: Prince of Yuanling Shuxing, styled Zitui, was Emperor Gaozong's twenty-sixth son.

s0296.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was established as Prince of Yuanling.
s0296.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he was made prince of Yuanling.

s0297.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass.
s0297.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass.

s0298.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was attendant for matters.
s0298.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye era he was attendant for matters.

s0299.literal: Prince of Yueshan Shushao, styled Ziqin, was the twenty-seventh son of Emperor Gaozong.
s0299.idiomatic: Prince of Yueshan Shushao, styled Ziqin, was Emperor Gaozong's twenty-seventh son.

s0300.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was established as Prince of Yueshan; soon he was wise-martial general, with aides and clerks.
s0300.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he was made prince of Yueshan; soon he was wise-martial general, with a staff.
